item.title: Mending a Well-Used Garment
item.description: Learn to describe damage, choose fabric for a repair, and keep a favourite coat or shirt in use for longer.

children.definition: A line where two pieces of fabric are sewn together.
children.example: When I turned my old coat inside out, I saw that the side seam had split while the fabric on either side was still sound.

children.definition: A piece of fabric attached to a damaged area to cover it.
children.example: I covered the hole at the elbow of my coat with a denim patch from an old pair of jeans.

children.definition: A single loop or length of thread made by passing a needle through fabric.
children.example: One stitch came loose at the corner of the patch on my coat, so I secured that corner again.

children.definition: The process of filling a hole in fabric by weaving new thread across it.
children.example: Darning the small hole in my coat meant laying threads across the gap and weaving more thread through them.

children.definition: The finished edge at the bottom of a garment or sleeve, made by turning the fabric under and sewing it in place.
children.example: The hem of my coat had come undone, and the folded fabric hung below the bottom edge.

children.definition: A split in fabric caused by pulling it or catching it on something.
children.example: My coat caught on a gate, leaving a short tear across the sleeve.

children.definition: To come apart as loops of yarn or sewing come undone in sequence.
children.example: The knitted cuff on my coat began to unravel after a loop caught on the zip.
collocations: a knitted edge starts to unravel

children.definition: To make an area of a garment stronger so it can withstand repeated use.
children.example: I used a strip of cotton to reinforce the pocket opening on my coat before the thin fabric gave way.

children.definition: A change to a garment's size or shape so that it fits better.
children.example: My second-hand coat needed one alteration before winter because the sleeves covered my hands.
children.translation_uz: kiyimning oʻlchami yoki bichimini moslab oʻzgartirish

children.definition: The strip of fabric between the line of sewing and the cut edge of the fabric.
children.example: There was enough seam allowance inside my old coat to make it a little wider at the waist.

children.definition: A piece of material left after a larger piece has been cut to size.
children.example: I saved a cotton offcut from a curtain I had shortened and later used it to mend my coat pocket.

children.definition: A separate layer of fabric sewn inside a garment to cover its inner surface.
children.example: The outer fabric of my coat was still in good shape, but the lining had split near the shoulder.

children.definition: To develop a ragged edge as individual threads in woven fabric come loose.
children.example: The fabric at the edge of my coat pocket began to fray where my keys rubbed against it.

children.definition: To restore damaged fabric or a damaged garment to a usable state.
children.example: I decided to mend my winter coat after a tear appeared near the pocket.
